canada.title: MDs raise concerns about patient waits, closures at Dynacare labs
canada.summary: As bargaining between Dynacare and its 350 unionized laboratory workers stalls, Manitoba doctors are raising “significant concerns” about patients struggling to get tests done.

canada.title: B.C. RCMP Major Crimes officer charged with accessing child sexual abuse material
canada.summary: A B.C. RCMP Major Crimes officer has been charged with one count of accessing child sexual abuse and exploitation material, according to the B.C. Prosecution Service (BCPS).

canada.summary: Leeway program threatened as territorial government proposes to remove rent caps, reintroduce no-cause evictions

canada.title: Drawn lot decides mayor of Lytton, B.C., after votes are tied at 45 each
canada.summary: The new mayor in Lytton, B.C., a tiny village razed by a raging wildfire in 2021, has been determined by the drawing of lots after a tied election.

canada.title: Vancouver Aquarium says goodbye to beloved sloth Hurricane, dead at 29
canada.summary: VANCOUVER - Hurricane, the sloth that has been hanging out at the Vancouver Aquarium for years, has died at the age of 29.

canada.title: Alberta UCP officials, candidates must now sign pro-Canada pledge form
canada.summary: Danielle Smith says anyone who wants to run for the party in next year's election will also have to affirm pro-Canada views.

canada.title: Saskatchewan throne speech paints province as strong and steady during global uncertainty
canada.summary: "The world is uncertain," said Lt.-Gov. Bernadette McIntyre, as she opened her speech on Tuesday. "Saskatchewan isn't."

canada.title: RCMP investigating allegations of money laundering, fraud in Alberta health procurement probes
canada.summary: The ongoing RCMP investigation into procurement processes and practices at Alberta Health and Alberta Health Services involves an investigation into alleged fraud, breach of trust, and money laundering, according to a letter filed in court earlier this month.

canada.title: Fires spark teardown of Pepsi Park encampment in Regina
canada.summary: Regina Fire and Protective Services says it responded to four fires in four days at Pepsi Park in the lead-up to the encampment being dismantled on Tuesday. Advocates say people living there should have been warned.

canada.title: Central Labrador families frustrated amid ‘unexpected’ school bus driver shortage
canada.summary: School transportation service in the Upper Lake Melville region of Labrador is expected to run as normal Wednesday after students were left without a bus Tuesday.

canada.title: Nearly 200 First Nations leaders, the prime minister and premiers gathered for a historic meeting about almost everything. Now what?
canada.summary: First Nations finally got a first ministers’ meeting of their own. They left with money and promises, but what's next?

canada.title: Cowichan Tribes to propose solution protecting private property in January: lawyer
canada.summary: The lawyer for the Cowichan Tribes says they will make a proposal in January that protects private property rights.

canada.title: Yellowknife RCMP say missing woman found safe
canada.summary: Police say Chelsey Normandin, 35, was last seen on Oct. 20 and reported missing Monday afternoon. She was found safe on Tuesday, hours after RCMP asked for help to find her.

canada.title: EverWind proposes binding agreement with N.S. on data centre rules
canada.summary: The company that wants to build $8-billion-worth of data centres in Point Tupper, N.S., says it’s offered to sign an agreement with the province to hold it to its promises.

canada.title: Ford says he feels 'badly' for students caught up in his government's career college OSAP pause
canada.summary: On the first day back after a 147-day break from the Ontario legislature, provincial opposition parties spent much of question period calling for colleges and universities minister Nolan Quinn to be fired for his handling of the OSAP program.

canada.title: Former Ontario cabinet minister who resigned over expenses scandal defends promotion
canada.summary: A former member of Ontario Premier Doug Ford's cabinet who resigned his post over an expenses scandal is defending his recent promotion.

canada.title: Nova Scotia Power appoints new president and CEO after announced departure of current head
canada.summary: Chris Smith, Nova Scotia Power's current executive vice-president, will take over the helm next week from Vivek Sood, who is departing at the end of his one-year contract.
canada.outlet: CBC News, Global News, Halifax Examiner

canada.title: Premier-designate Doerkson was appointed — not elected — interim leader of the party. What happens next?
canada.summary: The Conservative Party of B.C. has said it would have to "pursue the appropriate means" under the party's constitution in order for leader, and now premier-designate, Lorne Doerkson to keep the top job after the provincial election — but it's unclear if that's happened.
canada.outlet: CBC News, Global News, The Tyee
